lessons.title: A King and His People
lessons.context: A short literary passage about a wise king.

paragraphs.urdu: پرانے زمانے میں ایک بادشاہ اپنی رعایا سے بہت محبت کرتا تھا۔
paragraphs.en: In old times a king loved his subjects very much.

paragraphs.urdu: وہ ہر مہینے اپنے لباس بدل کر شہر میں جاتا تھا تاکہ لوگوں کی زندگی دیکھ سکے۔
paragraphs.en: He would change his clothes every month and go into the city so he could see the people's lives.

paragraphs.urdu: ایک دن اس نے دیکھا کہ ایک بوڑھا آدمی بھوکا بیٹھا ہے۔
paragraphs.en: One day he saw an old man sitting hungry.

paragraphs.urdu: بادشاہ نے جلدی سے اپنے وزیروں کو حکم دیا کہ غریبوں کی مدد کی جائے۔
paragraphs.en: The king quickly ordered his ministers that the poor be helped.

paragraphs.urdu: اسی انصاف اور شفقت کی وجہ سے لوگ آج بھی اس بادشاہ کو یاد کرتے ہیں۔
paragraphs.en: Because of this same justice and compassion, people still remember this king today.

questions.question: What would the king do every month?
options: Change clothes and go into the city

questions.question: Why did he go into the city?
What did he see one day?
Why do people still remember this king?

lessons.title: The Poet's Garden
lessons.context: A short literary passage about a poet finding inspiration.

paragraphs.urdu: وہ شاعر ہر صبح اپنے باغ میں بیٹھ کر شعر لکھتا تھا۔
paragraphs.en: That poet would sit in his garden every morning and write verses.

paragraphs.urdu: پھولوں کی خوشبو اور پرندوں کی آواز اسے نئے خیال دیتی تھی۔
paragraphs.en: The fragrance of flowers and the sound of birds gave him new ideas.

paragraphs.urdu: جہاں الفاظ ختم ہو جاتے تھے وہاں وہ خاموشی سے فطرت کو دیکھتا رہتا تھا۔
paragraphs.en: Where words ran out, he would keep silently watching nature.

paragraphs.urdu: اس کے شعر سادہ تھے لیکن ان میں زندگی کی گہری حکمت پوشیدہ تھی۔
paragraphs.en: His verses were simple but they held life's deep wisdom hidden within them.

paragraphs.urdu: لوگ کہتے تھے کہ اس کا باغ نہیں بلکہ اس کا دل شاعری کا اصل گھر تھا۔
paragraphs.en: People said that it was not his garden but his heart that was poetry's true home.

questions.question: Where would the poet write verses every morning?
What gave him new ideas?
options: The fragrance of flowers and sound of birds

questions.question: What did his verses hold, according to the passage?
What did people say was poetry's true home?
